meta.name: RPSGT Scoring Lab Phase 3 mini-study
meta.sourceBasis: The mini-study reuses original Sleep Pathways Guild schematic staging epochs and scoring-context cases to teach sequential review without embedding patient recordings, proprietary scoring-manual figures, or copied textbook figures.
meta.clinicalBoundary: The sequence is pedagogic rather than a model of mandatory sleep architecture. Real scoring requires the current official AASM Scoring Manual, the complete recording, facility procedures, and supervised scorer training.

epochs.rationale: Wake-oriented posterior alpha, eye activity, and relatively higher chin tone support the intended teaching pattern.
Low-amplitude mixed/theta-oriented EEG, slow eye movements, and the absence of N2 teaching morphology support the intended N1 pattern.
The schematic K-complex and spindle region support the intended N2 teaching pattern.
Neighboring context does not replace the current epoch evidence; the N2 teaching morphology remains present.
Prominent frontal slow-wave teaching activity supports the intended N3 pattern.
The current epoch continues the deep-NREM teaching pattern rather than being restaged only because a transition follows later.
The displayed epoch returns to N2-oriented morphology with a lower-amplitude background and N2 teaching features.
The schematic emphasizes an N1-oriented background and slow eye movements without an N2 teaching marker.
Low-amplitude mixed-frequency EEG, rapid eye movements, and low chin tone support the intended REM teaching pattern.
The current epoch retains the REM teaching relationship; a later transition does not change the evidence within this epoch.
The schematic again shows N2 teaching morphology after the REM-oriented interval.
Posterior alpha, eye activity, and higher chin tone support the intended wake teaching pattern at the end of the sequence.

contextStops.label: Arousal context stop
contextStops.focus: Pause the stage sequence and judge a full-montage arousal pattern before continuing.

contextStops.label: Limb-movement context stop
contextStops.focus: Use the longer montage to judge movement-series context rather than a single burst in isolation.

contextStops.label: Respiratory boundary context stop
contextStops.focus: Use the thermal airflow and respiratory-effort channels to identify one continuous adult apnea across the epoch boundary.

reference: Robertson, B., Marshall, B., & Carno, M.-A. (2014). Polysomnography for the sleep technologist: Instrumentation, monitoring, and related procedures. Elsevier. American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). The AASM manual for the scoring of sleep and associated events (Version 3). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
